winter's.linePrev: 1 ContributorSign LyricsI was born in Montreal
winter's.line: A winter’s slip that bloomed in fall
winter's.lineNext: Due my father’s lot in life
stanza: 1 ContributorSign LyricsI was born in Montreal
A winter’s slip that bloomed in fall
Due my father’s lot in life
I got his name and I killed his wife
As if her blood I’d broken through
Had never been enough for two…
So I was sent out early on
To cutting black ice on the pond
To lying flat and pulling free
Whatever might rise up to me

winter's.linePrev: So many people with so much to do
winter's.line: The winter's so cold, my hands turn blue
winter's.lineNext: Old men sleeping on the filthy ground
stanza: So many people with so much to do
The winter's so cold, my hands turn blue
Old men sleeping on the filthy ground
They spend their whole day just walking around
Nobody else here seems to care
They walk right past them like they ain't even there
Am I the last of my kind?
Am I the last of my kind?

winter's.linePrev: Fear no more the heat o' th' sun
winter's.lineNext: Thou thy worldly task hast done
stanza: Fear no more the heat o' th' sun
Nor the furious winter's rages
Thou thy worldly task hast done
Home art gone, and ta'en thy wages
Golden lads and girls all must
As chimney-sweepers, come to dust

winter's.linePrev: Like a long ago Sunday when I walked through the alley
winter's.line: On a cold winter's morning to a church house
stanza: Lyrically, this song is classic Prine, whose “stuff” Bob Dylan once said: it’s…
Like a long ago Sunday when I walked through the alley
On a cold winter's morning to a church house
Just to shovel some snow

winter's.line: We sailed away on a winter's day
winter's.lineNext: With fate as malleable as clay
stanza: We sailed away on a winter's day
With fate as malleable as clay
But ships are fallible, I say
And the nautical, like all things, fades
And I can recall our caravel:
A little wicker beetle shell
With four fine masts and lateen sails
Its bearings on Cair Paravel

winter's.lineNext: In a deep and dark December
stanza: A winter's day
In a deep and dark December
I am alone
Gazing from my window
To the streets below
On a freshly fallen, silent shroud of snow

winter's.lineNext: I hear that high and lonesome sound
stanza: Winter’s nigh and summer’s o’er
I hear that high and lonesome sound
Of my husband coming for
To bring me home to Hadestown
Way down Hadestown
Way down under the ground
